experiences.name: Tacos al Pastor Crawl in La Condesa

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Tour

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at ACDMX airport at 13:00. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station (very budget-friendly at ~5 MXN) to the city center. Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico. Once settled, take a leisurely orientation walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución) — one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace exterior for free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina, a lively pedestrian street in Centro Histórico filled with street food stalls and local atmosphere. Explore the surrounding streets and get a feel for the neighborhood nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Stop at a local taquería near the Zócalo — try tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor for around 15–25 MXN each. Look for spots with high local foot traffic.
meals.dinner: Head to Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén or a nearby fondita (family-run eatery) on Calle Uruguay for a comida corrida (set meal with soup, main, and drink) for around 80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some cash at a bank ATM rather than at the airport to get better rates. Keep your belongings secure in crowded areas. The Metro is the cheapest and fastest way to get around — buy a rechargeable card.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN), the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán located right next to the Zócalo. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and the excellent on-site museum included in the ticket price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio Nacional (National Palace) — entry is FREE. Marvel at Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history on the grand staircase. Afterward, explore the historic streets of Centro Histórico, including the beautiful Palacio de Bellas Artes exterior and Alameda Central park, both free to enjoy.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela, a large crafts market nearby, for souvenir browsing (no obligation to buy). Then enjoy the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico at night — the buildings are beautifully lit.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh tamales and atole (warm corn drink) from a street vendor near the hotel for around 30–50 MXN total — a classic Mexico City morning tradition.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local comedor inside Mercado de San Juan (Mercado Internacional de Artesanías area) for an affordable set lunch around 80–100 MXN.
meals.dinner: Try a torta (Mexican sandwich) or tlayuda from a street stall on Eje Central Lázaro Cárdenas near Bellas Artes for 40–70 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Palacio Nacional is free but requires showing ID at the entrance. Arrive at Templo Mayor when it opens (Tuesday–Sunday, 9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Tuesdays are free entry for Mexican nationals but still affordable for visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán (Line 3 to Viveros station), one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian neighborhoods. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance (~270 MXN). Spend the morning exploring this iconic cultural landmark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Coyoacán to the central Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo. Browse the weekend-style artisan market stalls around the plaza. Visit the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for local snacks and a taste of authentic neighborhood life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Visit the rooftop terrace bar at a nearby hostel or budget hotel for affordable drinks with views of the city skyline, or simply enjoy a walk along the illuminated Madero pedestrian street.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a café near your hotel before heading out — try chilaquiles (tortilla chips in salsa with egg) at a local breakfast spot for around 60–90 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — try enfrijoladas, tostadas de tinga, or fresh aguas frescas. A full meal costs around 80–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro Histórico, visit a taquería on Calle Mesones or nearby streets for tacos de guisado (stewed meat tacos) at 20–30 MXN each.

day_by_day.notes: The Frida Kahlo Museum sells out quickly — book tickets online at least a week in advance. Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists during the day. The Metro ride costs only ~5 MXN each way.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Insurgentes station and walk to the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the world's greatest anthropology museums (entry ~85 MXN). Spend 2–3 hours exploring pre-Columbian civilizations, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — entry is FREE. This massive urban park is perfect for a relaxed afternoon stroll. Visit Lago de Chapultepec and enjoy the atmosphere. Optionally, view the exterior of Chapultepec Castle (entry ~85 MXN if budget allows) for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Condesa or Roma Norte neighborhood (Metro to Insurgentes or Sonora). Walk along Avenida Ámsterdam (a circular tree-lined boulevard) and browse local shops and street art. These neighborhoods offer great people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh fruit, yogurt, and granola from a local tianguis (street market) near the hotel for under 40 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat near Chapultepec — look for fonditas or loncheras (lunch spots) on side streets off Avenida Constituyentes for a set meal around 90–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: In Roma Norte, try a budget-friendly taquería — El Turix (cochinita pibil tacos) is legendary and very affordable at around 25–35 MXN per taco.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is massive — wear comfortable shoes. Sundays are free entry for all visitors, but since today is Thursday, the regular fee applies. Chapultepec Forest is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced, one of the largest and most authentic traditional markets in Mexico City, just a short Metro or walk from Centro Histórico. Explore the stalls selling spices, chiles, produce, street food, and local goods — a true feast for the senses and completely free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Barrio de Tepito area murals or visit the lesser-known but stunning Museo de la Ciudad de México (Museum of Mexico City) — entry is FREE. This museum is housed in a beautiful colonial palace and tells the story of the city's history. Spend your final afternoon revisiting any favorite spots in Centro Histórico or picking up last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final night with a special but still budget-friendly dinner. Head to a local cantina in Centro Histórico for a traditional Mexican meal with live mariachi music — many cantinas offer free botanas (snacks) with drink orders. End the night with a walk along the beautifully lit Zócalo.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a classic Mexico City breakfast at a market stall in La Merced — try huaraches (thick oval masa topped with beans and salsa) for around 40–60 MXN.
meals.lunch: Grab street tacos or a torta from vendors around Centro Histórico for a light and cheap lunch (50–80 MXN total) to save room for a special dinner.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night at a traditional cantina like Salón Corona or a similar local institution in Centro Histórico — budget around 150–250 MXN for food and a couple of drinks.

day_by_day.notes: La Merced market is best visited in the morning when it is most active. Keep valuables secure in busy market areas. If your departure flight is early the next day, pack your bags tonight and confirm your airport transport — the Metro is the most budget-friendly option (Line 1 from Centro Histórico toward the airport).

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approx. 45–60 min by taxi or Uber). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walking tour of the immediate surroundings: stroll through the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), admire the façade of the Palacio Nacional and the Metropolitan Cathedral. Pop into the covered arcade of the Portal de Mercaderes for a first taste of local street life. Keep the pace relaxed after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero and watch the city light up at dusk. Head to the Mirador of the Torre Latinoamericana (small entry fee) for panoramic night views of the city skyline — a perfect low-effort, high-reward first evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Skipped / light snack on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick late lunch near the Zócalo at Café El Popular — a classic 24-hour diner serving comida corrida (set lunch menu) with soup, rice, main dish, and drink for around MXN 120–160. Affordable and authentic.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Bar El Cardenal (Centro Histórico location) — a beloved mid-range institution known for traditional Mexican cuisine. Try the caldo tlalpeño, chiles en nogada (seasonal) or mole dishes. Budget approx. MXN 300–450 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Altitude in Mexico City is ~2,240 m — stay hydrated and avoid overexertion on arrival day. Exchange some cash at the airport or use an ATM near the hotel for small vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its excellent on-site museum (Museo del Templo Mayor). This Aztec ceremonial center sits just steps from the Zócalo and offers deep insight into pre-Hispanic culture. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Entry approx. MXN 85.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio Nacional to view Diego Rivera's iconic murals depicting Mexican history — free entry with ID. Afterward, head to Mercado de San Juan (15-min walk) to browse artisan foods, imported cheeses, charcuterie, fresh juices, and local specialties. A great cultural and culinary immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the hip Barrio Alameda area near Alameda Central park. Visit the Museo Franz Mayer (decorative arts and applied design, MXN 65 entry) if open late, or simply stroll the park. End the night with live music at a cantina in the Centro — try Cantina La Peninsular or Bar La Ópera for atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby at Café de Tacuba — a historic restaurant open since 1912, serving tamales, atole, and traditional Mexican breakfast plates. Budget MXN 150–220.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan — graze the stalls for tacos de canasta, fresh ceviche tostadas, and agua fresca. Budget MXN 100–180 total.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico (inside Hotel Downtown) — refined Mexican cuisine in a beautiful open-air courtyard. Try the sopa azteca and regional mole. Budget MXN 350–500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Templo Mayor and Palacio Nacional are both free or low-cost and within walking distance of each other. Wear comfortable shoes — today is a walking-heavy day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — one of the most impressive archaeological sites in the Americas. Take an organized shared shuttle or public bus from Terminal Norte (Metro to Autobuses del Norte, then ADO/Teotihuacán bus, ~1 hr, MXN 60–80 each way). Arrive early to beat crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead. Allow 3–4 hours on site. Entry MXN 90.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico by early afternoon. Rest briefly at the hotel, then visit the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) — housed in a stunning Neoclassical building, showcasing Mexican art from the 16th–20th centuries. Entry MXN 85, free on Sundays.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the illuminated historic streets around Plaza Santo Domingo — one of the oldest squares in the Americas. Enjoy the colonial architecture and evening atmosphere. Optionally catch a performance at the Palacio de Bellas Artes (check schedule in advance — tickets MXN 150–500 depending on show).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab fresh tamales and atole from street vendors near the hotel or a nearby market stall. Budget MXN 50–80.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Teotihuacán — eat at one of the restaurants along the site perimeter such as La Gruta (a cave restaurant, atmospheric and mid-range, MXN 250–400) or pack snacks from the market.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Limosneros — a celebrated restaurant near the Zócalo serving creative takes on pre-Hispanic and colonial Mexican ingredients. Excellent mezcal selection. Budget MXN 400–550 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start Teotihuacán as early as possible (site opens at 9:00 AM) — it gets crowded and hot midday. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. March weather is typically dry and sunny with mild temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the neighborhoods of Coyoacán and San Ángel — take the Metro or Uber (approx. 30–40 min from Centro). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance as it sells out. The iconic blue house and its gardens are a cultural highlight. Entry MXN 270.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for tostadas de tinga, churros, and fresh fruit. Browse the artisan market in the Jardín del Centenario. Then head to San Ángel's Bazar del Sábado (if visiting on Saturday) for handmade crafts, jewelry, and folk art — great for mid-range souvenirs. Also explore the Museo Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico. Spend the evening exploring the nightlife and cultural scene around República de Uruguay and surrounding streets. Visit a pulquería — try Pulquería Las Duelistas, one of the oldest in the city — for a uniquely Mexican fermented drink experience in an authentic setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Coyoacán at Café El Jarocho — a legendary local coffee stand serving café de olla and fresh pastries. Standing room, very affordable. Budget MXN 40–70.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de Coyoacán — tostadas at the famous Tostadas Coyoacán stalls. A local institution. Budget MXN 120–180.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Los Danzantes in Coyoacán (before heading back) — upscale-casual Mexican cuisine with a strong mezcal and tequila program. Try the duck in mole negro. Budget MXN 400–550 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets at least 2–3 days in advance via their official website — walk-in entry is rarely available. The Bazar del Sábado in San Ángel only operates on Saturdays; if Day 4 is not a Saturday, replace with a visit to the Museo de Arte Carrillo Gil instead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Centro Histórico — visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Abelardo Rodríguez, two authentic local markets near the hotel. Explore the food stalls, spice vendors, and daily life of Mexico City residents. A great immersive cultural experience with no entry fee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo de la Ciudad de México (City Museum), housed in a beautiful colonial palace just off the Zócalo — traces the full history of Mexico City from Aztec times to the present. Entry free or minimal fee. Afterward, do any last-minute souvenir shopping along Calle Moneda or near the Zócalo. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the neighborhood — celebrate the trip with a special meal. If budget allows, splurge slightly at Contramar (book ahead) or keep it local and heartfelt at a neighborhood fonda. End with a walk along the illuminated Zócalo one last time.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Mexican breakfast at the hotel or at a nearby fonda — chilaquiles verdes or rojos with eggs, beans, and fresh orange juice. Budget MXN 120–180.
meals.lunch: Tacos al pastor from a trusted street taquería near the Mercado — El Huequito (founded 1959, credited with inventing tacos al pastor) is steps from the hotel. Budget MXN 80–130.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurante Nicos (if willing to travel slightly) or stay local at Fonda El Refugio in Centro — classic regional Mexican dishes in a warm, unpretentious setting. Budget MXN 300–450 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is early on Day 6, plan to pack on the evening of Day 5. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transit and security. Uber or pre-booked taxi from Centro to AICM airport is recommended over Metro with luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer via luxury sedan to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of Centro Histórico's UNESCO World Heritage core: Plaza de la Constitución (Zócalo), the magnificent Metropolitan Cathedral, and the Templo Mayor archaeological site with an expert archaeologist guide. Explore the Palacio Nacional to admire Diego Rivera's sweeping murals up close.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico as the historic buildings glow at dusk. Aperitivo at the rooftop bar of Hotel Downtown or Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for panoramic Zócalo views.

meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel or a quick stop at Azul Histórico — a refined courtyard restaurant serving elevated Mexican classics using heirloom ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Limosneros, one of Mexico City's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants steps from the hotel, showcasing pre-Hispanic ingredients in contemporary tasting menus with expertly paired mezcals

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm Templo Mayor hours (closed Mondays). Keep the afternoon relaxed given travel fatigue — the walking tour is leisurely paced.

day_by_day.morning: Private early-access visit to the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec (arrange VIP entry before public opening). Spend 2–3 hours with a dedicated cultural guide exploring the Aztec Sun Stone, Maya galleries, and Olmec colossal heads. This is considered one of the world's greatest anthropology museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood: browse the tree-lined Presidente Masaryk boulevard, visit the Soumaya Museum (free entry, stunning architecture housing a vast art collection including Rodin sculptures), and enjoy a leisurely window-shopping walk through luxury boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via private car. Visit the iconic Bar La Opera (est. 1876) for a classic cocktail and to see the bullet hole in the ceiling allegedly made by Pancho Villa. Then head to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café de Tacuba, a legendary 1912 institution in Centro Histórico serving traditional Mexican morning dishes like chilaquiles and tamales in a stunning tiled colonial setting
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pujol's casual sister concept or at Quintonil in Polanco — both are world-ranked restaurants; Quintonil focuses on seasonal Mexican vegetables and local ingredients in a refined, intimate space
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol, consistently ranked among the world's top 20 restaurants — Chef Enrique Olvera's iconic tasting menu featuring the legendary 'Mole Madre' aged over 1,000 days is a once-in-a-lifetime culinary experience (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Pujol reservations must be made weeks in advance — confirm before travel. Private car recommended for Polanco visit. Soumaya Museum is free but donations appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient 'City of the Gods' (approx. 50 km northeast of the city, 1-hour drive). Arrive early to beat crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon with an expert archaeologist, explore the Avenue of the Dead, and visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl. Option to arrange a private hot-air balloon flight over the pyramids at sunrise for a truly extraordinary experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city. Visit the Museo Dolores Olmedo or stop at a renowned mezcal boutique in Roma Norte for a curated private tasting of artisanal mezcals and tequilas, learning about production regions and agave varieties.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the bohemian neighborhoods of Roma Norte and Condesa on a private food walk — sampling street tacos at top-rated taquerías, elote (corn), and churros with chocolate. These neighborhoods are the epicenter of Mexico City's vibrant food scene.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the hotel for the Teotihuacán excursion, or breakfast at the site's La Gruta restaurant — a dramatic cave restaurant inside a natural cavern near the pyramids
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Gruta restaurant at Teotihuacán — a unique dining experience inside an illuminated natural cave with traditional Mexican cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rosetta in Roma Norte — Chef Elena Reygadas' flagship restaurant in a restored 19th-century mansion, blending Italian technique with Mexican ingredients; winner of Latin America's Best Female Chef award

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán no later than 7:30 AM to arrive before crowds and heat. Hot-air balloon must be booked in advance through operators like Globos Bex. Wear comfortable shoes for pyramid climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to Xochimilco's ancient floating gardens (chinampas) via a decorated trajinera (flower boat) with a private guide. Learn about the pre-Aztec agricultural system still in use today. Optional add-on: visit an axolotl conservation sanctuary on the chinampas. This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Mexico City's most unique cultural experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul — the Blue House) in Coyoacán, Frida Kahlo's birthplace and home. Explore her intimate studio, personal belongings, and art. Afterward, wander through the charming cobblestone streets and plazas of Coyoacán, one of the city's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhoods. Browse artisan markets and local craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with a renowned Mexico City chef — learn to make traditional dishes such as mole negro, tamales, and agua fresca from scratch using ingredients sourced from local markets. This immersive 3-hour class concludes with eating your own creations.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel's restaurant or at a local café in Centro Histórico before departing for Xochimilco
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served aboard your private trajinera on the Xochimilco canals — arranged by the hotel with local specialties, fresh fruit, and artisanal beverages
meals.dinner: Dinner is the private cooking class meal itself, or follow up with dessert and digestifs at Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre in Coyoacán — a legendary, no-menu, no-sign mezcalería and kitchen serving rotating dishes based on what's available that day (a true insider experience)

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets well in advance — timed entry sells out quickly. Xochimilco is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Private trajinera hire recommended over shared boats for a premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de San Juan, a premium covered market in Centro Histórico beloved by chefs and food lovers — browse stalls of exotic cheeses, imported delicacies, fresh seafood, charcuterie, tropical fruits, and artisan products. Follow with a private tour of the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and the spectacular murals by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for leisure time, spa treatment if available, or a private chocolate and mezcal pairing experience arranged through a local artisan chocolatier. Optional: visit the Archivo Fotográfico Manuel Toussaint or the stunning Biblioteca Vasconcelos (a visually breathtaking modern library) for architecture and culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Mexico City's most iconic fine-dining destinations, followed by a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated Zócalo — a perfect final image of one of the world's great cities.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the hotel — request a traditional Mexican breakfast spread including fresh juices, pan dulce, huevos rancheros, and café de olla (cinnamon-spiced coffee)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan — graze across multiple stalls for a curated tasting experience: fresh ceviche, tuna tostadas, artisan cheese, and fresh-cut tropical fruit; a true gourmet market experience
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Sud 777 in Pedregal — Chef Edgar Nuñez's landmark restaurant set in a stunning garden space, offering a sophisticated tasting menu rooted in Mexican biodiversity and seasonal produce, with an exceptional natural wine and mezcal program

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange private transfer accordingly. Mercado de San Juan is closed on Sundays — verify hours. Consider purchasing artisan gifts and local products at the market as souvenirs. Allow extra time for luggage and check-out.
